limitations: One invented assistant-authored prompt-development case created after observing the v4 DEV pre-operator-wait attribution defect. Not an independent test, human label, organizer GT, or evidence of general accuracy. No real conversation text or personal data is copied.

items.scenario: Long pre-operator queue with an explicit bot notice, followed by a clear operator greeting, immediate answer and full closure; no operator-created wait.

expected_results.rationale: The first operator reply greets in Russian and introduces the operator.
The client supplied the exact public page context, visible link and desired result before the operator joined.
Public event-program navigation requires neither identity verification nor a protected action.
The operator identifies the requested public link and the client confirms that both requested days are visible.
The operator is polite and provides the requested help; the client expresses no separate complaint about the queue.

The long delay occurred in the pre-operator queue and the bot warned about it. The operator then answered clearly, created no wait and caused no confusion. This checklist excludes first-response thresholds; it does not require an operator to pre-announce joining or repeat a bot queue notice.
The operator recaps the opened program, offers additional assistance and says farewell.
No operator insult, private paid offer or confidential disclosure is present.
